clue.text: Omega scores on prejudices

parts.note: omega is literally 'big O', the long O of the Greek alphabet
tries are scores in rugby

explanation.surface: The last letter of the Greek alphabet racks up points against bias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Omega' is split as O-mega, Greek for 'great O', so it gives BIG O.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigotries are instances of intolerant bias, plural like the clue's word.

clue.text: See 17
Win round against Scots boy

indicators.note: the word for win goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to win is to gain
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A Scottish lad gets a victory over the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gavin is a boy's name of Scottish origin, popular in Scotland.

clue.text: Integration with a Catholic possibly an untried scenario?

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written
RC stands for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: Merging with a Catholic might be a scenario nobody has yet tried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges INTEGRATION plus A plus RC into TERRA INCOGNITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for unknown land, so ground not yet explored or tried, loosely a scenario nobody has experienced.

clue.text: Charge a monkey per head?

parts.note: a monkey is a mischievous child, an imp
per head means each

explanation.surface: Is the price for a monkey so much per head?
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to bring a formal accusation against an official, a charge.

clue.text: Not a few could be leavers

indicators.note: could be says these letters may become another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Quite a number of people might turn out to be departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Several means more than two but not many, which is the same as not a few.

clue.text: Pity a girl that's not all there!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not all there means the word for a girl lacks a letter, here its last

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Sympathy for a young woman who is a little simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all there' cuts the final S from LASS, leaving LAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, used where one might say 'What a pity!'

clue.text: Literary baron not on with John Humphrey

indicators.note: not says the following little word is to be left out of the baron's name

parts.note: Edward Bulwer-Lytton, novelist, was made Baron Lytton
taken as written, the letters removed
Elton John, the singer, so John points to his first name

explanation.surface: A literary peer is not getting on with a man called John Humphrey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes ON from LYTTON to leave LYTT. Humphrey Lyttelton was a British jazz trumpeter and radio host.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Lyttelton, known as Humph, was a jazz trumpeter and long-running panel-show chairman, so his first name points to him.

clue.text: Evasive throw, about 12 ins

indicators.note: the word for throw goes round the measurement

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy
twelve inches make one foot, written 1 FT

explanation.surface: A dodgy throw comes within about a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 in 1 FT is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifty describes someone who seems deceitful and avoids straight answers.

clue.text: Select affairs with new logos about Aries and planet at church

indicators.note: the rearranged logos goes around the other pieces
new says the letters of logos take a fresh order

parts.note: Aries is the Ram of the zodiac
Mars is a planet

explanation.surface: Exclusive matters involve fresh logos for a star sign and a planet in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the fodder so it splits around the Ram, the planet and the church abbreviation. 'Select affairs' is a loose definition: the schools pick their pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar schools in Britain choose pupils by exam, so they are selective institutions.

clue.text: Queen finished with dog?

parts.note: R stands for Regina, queen
over means finished

explanation.surface: Is the Queen done with her pet?
explanation.definitionFit: Rover is a stock name for a pet dog, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Heartless Roman satirist interrupts coloratura singer

indicators.note: interrupts says the satirist breaks into the singer's name

parts.note: Adelina Patti was a famous coloratura soprano

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter

parts.note: Varro wrote Menippean satires in ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A Roman satirist, lacking heart, cuts in on a high-flying soprano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle letter of the satirist's name; 'interrupts' then puts what is left inside the soprano's surname. 'Coloratura' works as a noun here, a coloratura soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: Luciano Pavarotti was the celebrated Italian operatic tenor.

clue.text: Blast the inconstant Arabs!

annotationWithheld.why: Blast the inconstant Arabs! (7): TANTARA is hidden in 'inconstant Arabs', the indicator being the 'in' of 'inconstant', so one clue word is both indicator and fodder.

clue.text: Right about the central light of ballet

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right goes round the light

parts.note: amber is the middle light of a traffic signal

explanation.surface: A dancer is right about the middle lamp of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambert is a British ballet company, founded by Marie Rambert.

clue.text: No shade for man in case containing article? Far from it

parts.note: taken as written
a tint is a shade of colour
he refers to a man

indicators.note: the word for in case holds the article

parts.note: lest means in case
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A man without colour sits in a box with something inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Not in the least means not at all, the same emphatic denial as far from it.

clue.text: Bearer of sacred object to sacred building outside circle

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the building goes outside the circle

parts.note: a temple is a sacred building
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone carrying a holy relic takes it to a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem pole is a carved post that carries totems, sacred emblems.

clue.text: Bearer one leaves when a singer

indicators.note: one, the letter I, departs from the word for bearer

parts.note: a carrier bears things
as means when

explanation.surface: A porter quits, once someone starts singing.
explanation.definitionFit: José Carreras is a Spanish operatic tenor, one of the Three Tenors.

clue.text: 11, 16 and 21 with 2 10 or Sandra, right away apart from one wrong note

parts.note: the figure 2 spelt out
the figure 10 spelt out
taken as written

indicators.note: right away says R, short for right, is dropped from the name

parts.note: taken as written before the letter goes
bar means apart from, except
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of note are jumbled

explanation.surface: The famous trio, plus Sandra, sing one wrong note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the four letters of the last word. The famous trio is 11, 16 and 21; Domingo later sang baritone roles, which makes him the odd one out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Three Tenors, Pavarotti, Carreras and Domingo, with Domingo latterly a baritone.

clue.text: He achieved his ton vulgarly, the selfish fellow

indicators.note: vulgarly suggests Cockney speech dropping the h-sounds of he and his

parts.note: taken as written before losing its h
got means achieved
taken as written before losing its h

explanation.surface: A conceited batsman who scored a hundred, put in common speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vulgarly' drops the H from both He and his, as in 'E GOT 'IS.
explanation.definitionFit: An egotist is a self-centred person who thinks only of himself.

clue.text: Died on the spot? That's not very nice

parts.note: OB stands for obiit, Latin for died
the scene is the spot where something happens

explanation.surface: Someone dying on the spot is rather unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive or indecent, an emphatic version of unpleasant.

clue.text: Rum to issue when expected to win

parts.note: rum means odd or strange
a son is issue, a child

explanation.surface: A drink goes to the offspring as soon as winning is anticipated.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on is betting language for a favourite likely to win.

clue.text: Singer of note in cloak

indicators.note: in says the note sits within the cloak

parts.note: a domino is a loose hooded cloak worn at masquerades
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A famous performer wraps himself in a cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Plácido Domingo is a celebrated Spanish operatic tenor and baritone.

clue.text: Intriguing fellow at opening of Scottish border to monarch

parts.note: Sc is short for Scottish
a hem is a border on cloth
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the monarch

explanation.surface: A plotter stands at the start of the Scottish frontier, facing the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at opening of' puts SC at the front; ER is Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A schemer plots and intrigues, so an intriguing fellow in the sense of one who intrigues.

clue.text: Artist's model after a lot of dosh

indicators.note: after says the model letter comes behind
a lot of means most but not all of the word, losing its end

parts.note: dosh is British slang for money
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A painter's sitter follows a pile of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims MONEY to MONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: In coastal area, back hand doing less than 40 hours

indicators.note: in says the reversed hand sits within the coastal word

parts.note: the shore is the coastal strip

indicators.note: back says the word for hand is turned around

parts.note: mitt is slang for hand

explanation.surface: Down on the shore, with a backhand, someone is working fewer than forty hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MITT into TTIM, which goes into SHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: On short time means working fewer hours than a normal working week, typically forty.

clue.text: I have finished in Scotland (North included)

indicators.note: included says the letter goes within the Scots word

parts.note: ower is Scots for over, finished

explanation.surface: I have completed my time north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is what such a person would say: 'I have (this)'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who possesses something can say 'I have', so the phrase fits a possessor cryptically.

clue.text: Work with fingers said to be requirement

indicators.note: said to be tells us the word for working with fingers is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to knead dough is to work it with the fingers

explanation.surface: Kneading dough is a necessity.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is something required, a necessity.

clue.text: The right locations for a Shakespeare character

parts.note: taken as written
sites are locations

explanation.surface: The correct venues for staging a figure from the Bard.
explanation.definitionFit: Thersites is the scurrilous Greek in Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida.
